title: It isn’t for the few to tell the many what is true. We’re standing wi...
transcript: Ali Louis Bourzgui gave one of the best speeches of Tony's night, but because it made people with power uncomfortable, the official social media account of Lost Boys was made to take it down and CBS never even put it up. And this is not an attack on the show at all, but rather for those who saw Ali's speech and felt it was a threat and chose to prioritise their own comfort and pocket books rather than engage with conversation. Ali's speech was not an attack, but rather a reminder that the vampires of the world who take whether it be money or land or lives or individuality, will only succeed in losing their humanity. just saying that wanting Palestinians to live free and full and fruitful lives without occupation makes you uncomfortable, then I have to ask why do you not want that? Is the safety of your people only possible at the expense of others? He did not once blame Jewish people or even mention Israel. He didn't call for violence. The safety of one people should not imply nor come at the expense of another. And speaking for the people with the most need should not be seen as an inherent attack on the other. And if you honestly believe that Israel is more at risk right now than Palestine, then I thoroughly encourage you to look up photos and the death counts of both countries if you are a Jewish person. Living in America. Frankly, this piece about immigrants was much more about you specifically than either the colonizer bit or the Palestine bit. And I know the word colonizer gets thrown around a lot and it makes people antsy, but even if you consider all white people living in America to be colonizers, then I, as a white person living in America, will agree with all you. Still, I get no fulfilment from any land or lives that were stolen so that I can live here. There is still nothing about his speech that I disagree with. I have family in Israel too, because my grandfather and his brother were the only two members of my family on that side that survived the literal Holocaust. I get what it means to want your family to be safe, but me wanting their safety does not justify the violence that is being done to other families. A full thank you to Ali for standing up for what he believes in. I thought the speech was incredibly eloquent and well put. And shame on those who have chosen to silence his words rather than engage with them. If you are a producer on the show that has benefited from my content, thank you for helping me to create this piece of art I really resonated with. I encourage you to have the speech reinstated on the official social media platform. I think it's important for people to hear Conversation is always preferable to censorship, even when it makes us a little uncomfortable. And if you are a fan of the show and a fan of the words that Ali said, that I encourage you to find the speech on the platform still brave enough to share it and share it yourself. Boost it. It deserves to be heard.
